races.name: Honda Wakefield Super-n Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with solid good-ground form (sim-going 13/15, 3 wins, 7 places), drops back to 12f which he has won over before, and with Miss Chelsea Brooks claiming 5lb the weight is manageable; simply has to be caught from the front.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground and carries the stable confidence of Tim Easterby (T14: 3/81 is modest), a natural hold-up operator who finished runner-up most recently and will need to travel closer than ideal given the single pace-setter dominating at the front.

runners_data.name: Glitter Code
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell has been in good form (T14: 6/28) and this 4-year-old showed a decent second over 8f on good ground, but the hood suggests a horse that can be headstrong; 40 days off the track is a mild concern, and as a genuine hold-up type she needs more pace than this race is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's consistent mare has placed at 10f on good ground twice recently and naturally races prominently — she is the most likely horse to sit second behind Max Of Stars throughout and launch the first meaningful challenge; her 5lb claim from Miss Charli Parker is a legitimate asset.

runners_data.name: Anificas Beauty
runners_data.note: Two wins at 8f on good ground shows ability, but this is a true hold-up horse whose position on the map understates how far back she will actually race; in a race with one front-runner the slow early pace may rob her of the end-to-end tempo she needs, and the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 fairly tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old whose recent form includes a third over 10f on good ground, though the broader record is inconsistent; naturally a hold-up horse operating out of her comfort zone in this race shape, the STYLE_FIT warning (0.94) is apt and trainer Walford's T14 strike rate (2/12) offers limited confidence.

runners_data.name: The Pug
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's 6-year-old has headgear (p) and a patchy recent record including a U (unseated) — his true hold-up style is poorly suited to a lone-pace race where he cannot access sustained gallop, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) reflects how unlikely he is to produce his best in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Max Of Stars is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, he is set to dictate an unchallenged, controlled tempo over Pontefract's 1m2f on Good to Firm ground. Star Start is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and, while she may track Max Of Stars through the early stages, she lacks the authority to force a true test of stamina. Sunny Orange, Glitter Code, Anificas Beauty, Quirke On Parole, and The Pug are all natural hold-up horses, meaning the field will string out behind a single pace-setter with a comfortable lead — a shape that historically suits those who can travel close to or just behind the front-runner and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp late burst. This race shape squarely favours the prominent or close-tracking profile: a horse that can sit within two lengths of Max Of Stars and pounce before the hold-up brigade have time to wind up their finishes. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can place at the rear; Anificas Beauty, Quirke On Parole, and The Pug are the true closers, but in a race with only one pace-setter they are unlikely to see enough tempo to fully exploit their style, making Sunny Orange — the closest natural hold-up horse with course-ground form — the most credible threat to ambush from the first group back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Max Stars Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars is allowed to stride clear from the gate and control a steady, uncontested tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Max Of Stars sets a comfortable gallop and dictates every yard, with the rest strung out in his wake on Good to Firm ground; a horse that can track him in second or third and time a run off his back is best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting just off the steady pace tracks Max Of Stars into the straight and produces a decisive run before the hold-up horses hit top gear.
scenarios.body: Star Start or Sunny Orange, travelling smoothly in a handy berth, kicks past the leader at the two-furlong pole and holds on as the field finishes late; the steady gallop means the winner needs class rather than raw stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early and collapses in the straight, creating a bunched finish that delivers a late surge from the rear.
scenarios.body: Anificas Beauty or Glitter Code, though both are redistributed out of their natural rearward role, find the slow pace creates enough space for a strong closing run inside the final furlong; the style-fit penalty applies and this shape depends on an unusually compressed race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Max Of Stars goes too fast early, ties up before the final two furlongs, and the race turns chaotic for an outsider.
scenarios.body: A horse like Quirke On Parole or The Pug, already racing out of their natural hold-up role and mapped to midfield, gets lucky as the field fragments; both carry significant style-fit discounts and this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Max Of Stars is the only front-runner in the field — watch whether Miss Chelsea Brooks attempts to extend the lead aggressively early or settles for a crawl, as this single decision shapes every other runner's chance.

Star Start is the only horse likely to sit close to Max Of Stars throughout; if Miss Charli Parker misjudges the gap and leaves too much to do, the hold-up horses will not have enough pace to compensate — watch her early positioning out of the stalls.

Anificas Beauty, Quirke On Parole, and The Pug are all genuine hold-up types bunched together in the back half of the field; if they all need a strong pace that never materialises, they risk finishing in a cluster without landing a blow — monitor the early tempo carefully.
Glitter Code is 40 days off the track and wears a hood — watch her early in the race for any signs of greenness or over-keenness that could compromise her position and the race shape around her.

Good to Firm is confirmed for the 2:45 at Pontefract — no going concern for any runner, but the fast ground will ensure the race is run at a genuine clip once they turn for home, compressing the margin between tracking and hold-up styles in the final two furlongs.

races.name: Jayne - On Course Lady Bookmaker Ebf Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)
Riu Hotels And Resorts Ladies Day Veterans' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Spirit Genie
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who needs traffic to part and a strong pace to aim at; 0 wins and 0 places in 8 runs on similar good ground is a stark stat, and at 39 days off Jason Hart will need things to fall perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Returned a 32-day break winner on Standard going and has placed form at 8f, but seven runs on good ground have produced zero wins and only two places, which tempers any case for a step forward on this surface today.|

runners_data.name: Garden Oasis
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner at age 11 with an extraordinary 11-from-15 strike rate on comparable good ground, and Tim Easterby's stable is in decent nick (3/81 over 14 days); confirmed pacemaker whose ability to dictate terms uncontested is the defining tactical fact of this race.|

runners_data.name: Narmar
runners_data.note: Candlish runner whose last six starts show a tail-off in form (42-000), and while a genuine hold-up type, it is pushed forward to a mapped midfield position because the field is saturated with closers — racing out of its preferred rear slot (STYLE_FIT 0.91) further dims a modest recent profile.|

runners_data.name: Cosmos Raj
runners_data.note: Back just four days after finishing sixth at a longer trip, and although O'Meara has 3/52 over 14 days, this 8-year-old's true preference for hold-up racing is compromised by having to operate from a midfield map position (STYLE_FIT 0.93), with a form string of 957664 offering little encouragement.|

runners_data.name: Soames Forsyte
runners_data.note: Herrington's runner has placed just once in the last five — all on Standard ground — and today's good-to-firm conditions are 4/15 for the horse on comparable surfaces; its natural late-running style is squeezed by the crowded midfield redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.91), adding a positional layer to an already modest record.|

races.paceDynamic: Garden Oasis is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at age 11 with a strong recent record of making the running over this trip on good ground at Pontefract, will stride into an uncontested lead from the outset. With no genuine rival willing or able to challenge for the early lead, David Allan can set a controlled, sustainable gallop that suits a horse who has finished in the frame 11 times from 15 starts on comparable going. The hold-up contingent — Spirit Genie, Alessia Fernanda, Narmar, Cosmos Raj, and Soames Forsyte — will all be chasing the same late ground, creating traffic and positioning problems in the straight. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or lead profile: Garden Oasis controlling from the front or a horse tracking very close to it, with true hold-up types needing an unusually strong pace collapse that this lone, unhurried pace-setter is unlikely to produce. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can absorb at the rear — Narmar, Cosmos Raj, and Soames Forsyte are genuine closers but are mapped to midfield as they cannot all occupy their natural rearward berths, making their finishing kicks harder to deploy cleanly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Garden Oasis Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis is allowed to roll along at a measured gallop and no hold-up horse can find clear running in time.
scenarios.body: Garden Oasis dictates every yard on good-to-firm ground at a track it knows well, and the chasing pack spends the straight fighting for gaps rather than reeling in a horse already in rhythm; David Allan's experience over the Pontefract mile gives Garden Oasis an edge in managing the bend and the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fast enough to set up a strong late run and one closer finds clear daylight at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Spirit Genie or Alessia Fernanda, both with OK going profiles and placed form at 8f, pick up through traffic to catch a tiring Garden Oasis in the final 100 yards; this shape requires a pace that is quick enough to drain the leader, which is not guaranteed with an uncontested front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Garden Oasis over-extends early and fades sharply in the final two furlongs, opening the door for multiple late runners.
scenarios.body: This is the low-probability counter-scenario where a late-race scramble develops, but it depends on Garden Oasis setting a pace faster than its recent measured front-running efforts suggest; the redistributed hold-up types — Narmar, Cosmos Raj, Soames Forsyte — would need to find their true closing positions, which the crowded midfield makes structurally difficult.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a horse settles just off Garden Oasis's shoulder and pounces without needing a wide, deep hold-up run.
scenarios.body: None of the six runners is a natural second-slot tracker, so this shape requires tactical improvisation on the day; Alessia Fernanda, freshest of the closers at 32 days off, is the most likely to adapt and shadow the leader if the jockey reads the race quickly.

watchPoints.text: Garden Oasis (David Allan) breaks cleanly — if it does, it controls the race entirely; watch for any stumble or slow start that would hand the initiative to the chasing pack.|

Traffic congestion in the straight is a genuine risk with five hold-up horses all hunting the same gaps — Spirit Genie and Alessia Fernanda are the ones most likely to find daylight, or to get badly blocked.|
Cosmos Raj runs just four days after its last outing — watch for any signs of fatigue or under-recovery in the market or pre-race paddock behaviour that would further reduce an already slim chance.|

The confirmed good-to-firm going (reported for this race at 3:45) may increase pace in the early stages and slightly raise the probability of Scenario B if Garden Oasis responds to the fast surface by going faster than its usual controlled front-running tempo.|

Narmar and Soames Forsyte both return from 54 and 51 days off respectively — neither has strong recent form, but fresh-horse angles at this level occasionally fire; any market move for either would be worth noting before the off.|

races.name: Fbs Chartered Accountants Chaplins Club Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Betweenthesticks
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style performer with 11 placed efforts from 15 on similar going — James Sullivan's patient hold-just-off-pace approach suits this race perfectly and the horse arrives fresh enough on 29 days off.

runners_data.name: Le Beau Garcon
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who rarely wins but finds the frame; recent form is patchy with three finishes of 9th and 10th on similar going, and Joanna Mason will need significant pace-collapse to get competitive from the rear.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Applause
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has posted back-to-back 3rds on Good ground over 5-6f — David Allan will be looking to maximise late momentum off a strong gallop, though this horse needs things to fall right and has no wins from 10 similar-going runs.

runners_data.name: Sam's Xpress
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with modest recent form (8th, 5th, 9th latest), and with Sea Her Excel and The Tunguska Event also keen to lead, Dylan Hogan faces an immediate position battle that may drain this horse before the race is truly run.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Last won over 6f on Good ground (1 of 2 wins at similar going) and arrives just 4 days after its last run — naturally a hold-up horse but remapped to midfield given the surplus of closers, so its true late style is compromised by the race shape.

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Dual recent winner over 5f on Good ground and a natural front-runner who will contest for the early lead with Sam's Xpress and The Tunguska Event — Elle-May Croot's 5lb claim is a genuine asset if she can secure a clean break and manage the pace contest.

runners_data.name: Riffa Spirit
runners_data.note: Consistent without threatening on Good ground — four finishes between 3rd and 8th from the rear of the field — and Zak Wheatley will need an unusually clear passage to make an impact from a hold-up position here.

runners_data.name: Bibendum
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good ground last time and visored today, but naturally a hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map due to overcrowding at the rear — Ryan Sexton will need to adjust tactics, and the visor may encourage a more forward move than usual.

runners_data.name: Missmimi
runners_data.note: Returns from 256 days off which is a significant fitness concern, though she has won and placed on similar going; Tina Jackson's yard has limited recent form and Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim cannot fully offset the layoff risk at this level.

runners_data.name: The Tunguska Event
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner who won over 6f on Good ground and has hit the frame twice recently — Jason Hart will press for the lead from the off, but three-way pace rivalry risks burning out this 3yo before the final furlong, despite the visor sharpening early intent.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Her Excel, Sam's Xpress, and The Tunguska Event are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a fierce early pace over this Good to Firm 5f at Pontefract — there will be no soft lead and no tactical crawl. The three will battle for position from the off, likely burning each other out and compressing finishing times, which means the fractions will be honest and the final furlong will be a genuine test of residual stamina. Bibendum and Great are natural hold-up horses who have been remapped to midfield because the field is saturated with pace — they are unlikely to secure their preferred rear position, and should not be treated as genuine closers in this race shape. The race shape decisively favours horses who can travel prominently without leading — Betweenthesticks profiles as the clearest beneficiary — or those with the raw speed to pick up from midfield when the front three stop, rather than true hold-up runners who will struggle to thread through a compressed field late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out and a stalking prominent horse swoops in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sea Her Excel, Sam's Xpress, and The Tunguska Event set a furious gallop that sees each deteriorate in the closing stages, handing the race to a horse who travelled just off the pace under cover. Betweenthesticks, with strong form on Good ground and a proven ability to track pace and pounce, is the primary beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Melee
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters is fastest away, secures the rail, and controls fractions well enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: Despite the contested early pace, a front-runner with the most tactical ride can establish a small but crucial lead and dictate a rhythm that suits them, grinding rivals down. Sea Her Excel, who has won twice recently over this exact trip on Good ground and benefits from a 5lb claimer keeping the weight down, is best positioned to steal this scenario if the early scrapping plays into her hands.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Flyer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so intense that the race completely falls apart and a horse with a turn of foot from midfield picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A true burn-up between three pace-setters can occasionally create a vacuum that a quick-accelerating midfield horse exploits in the final 100 yards. Great and Bibendum, though remapped from their natural hold-up roles and racing out of position, are the types who could theoretically benefit — though their style-fit discount and redistribution means this shape is less reliable than it appears on paper.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that the entire field strings out and a late closer threads through on the far rail.
scenarios.body: In a race where the front three obliterate each other, a horse held up deepest could theoretically finish fastest of all, but this scenario is explicitly undermined by the fact that the genuine hold-up horses — Great and Bibendum — have been displaced to midfield and are not racing in their true role. Le Beau Garcon, who has recorded placed efforts off similar paces, is the most credible beneficiary if this unlikely shape emerges.

watchPoints.text: Sea Her Excel, Sam's Xpress, and The Tunguska Event — watch for a fierce early scramble for the lead that could see all three fight each other into the ground, dramatically reshaping the race by halfway.

Betweenthesticks — if James Sullivan settles this horse just off the early fracas on the inside, it is exceptionally well-placed to pounce; watch for its position leaving the stalls as a key pace-shape indicator.

Bibendum — wearing a visor and naturally a hold-up horse, Ryan Sexton may be tempted to push forward early given the surplus of closers behind; watch whether it contests the pace or drops back to its natural position.
Missmimi — 256 days off is a major flag for a horse now running in a fast-paced 5f sprint; watch market moves to gauge whether connections have given meaningful work signals ahead of this return.

Great — only 4 days since its last run and a natural hold-up type out of role; watch the early stages to see whether Shane Gray attempts to push forward or concedes ground and accepts a compromised position.

races.name: Bet With Jayne - Your Local Bookmaker Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 5yo owns back-to-back wins over this exact course and distance on Good ground; confirmed front-runner who will dictate here unopposed, though the STYLE_FIT tag suggests the P label slightly understates its lead tendencies and its chance could be trimmed in shapes that require it to race off a true gallop.

runners_data.name: Alfa Whiteburd
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's hold-up operator arrives with two wins in its last three and solid 6f Good-ground credentials; Jason Hart takes the ride and the horse's only requirement is that the pace holds all the way to the final furlong, which is plausible but not guaranteed from this configuration.

runners_data.name: Aberama Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent David O'Meara nine-year-old with three placed efforts on Good ground at this trip in recent form; wears a visor, travels prominently with Daniel Tudhope, and the fact its best historical effort here was a 20th suggests course idiosyncrasy should be noted despite solid recent placed form.

runners_data.name: Uppercase
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's improving four-year-old has won back-to-back over 7f on Good and Good to Soft but steps back to 6f here; Kaiya Fraser rides and the drop in trip is the key unknown — form figures show stamina rather than pure speed, so this furlong shorter tests whether it can quicken rather than grind.

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies hold-up type who won impressively over course and distance earlier in the season but has run poorly since, finishing 4th, 9th, 6th in subsequent starts; the visor is retained, David Allan rides, and only 7 days since last run is worth monitoring — best recent form gives it each-way claims but consistency is the concern.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's consistent seven-year-old shows an outstanding 11/15 sim-going record and a clean set of placed efforts on this surface; wears a hood, sits in the prominent group naturally, and David Nolan's familiarity with the stable is an asset — the trainer's 0/22 14-day record is a mild dampener.

runners_data.name: Mister Sox
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old has genuine pace credentials and a placed effort at this trip on Good ground, but the prominent positions are already spoken for and it is likely to find itself a length or two further back than ideal; Sean Kirrane rides, and the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that its chance is genuinely compromised by the race shape rather than its own ability ceiling.

runners_data.name: Sugar Baby
runners_data.note: Peter Niven's eight-year-old boasts three wins in its last five at this trip on Good ground — a strong statistic — but its natural front-running instincts will be squeezed out by the horses ahead of it in the queue; Ethan Tindall claims 5lbs which helps the weight, yet the horse needs to be in front or prominent to produce its best and the field shape makes that unlikely.

runners_data.name: Willolarupi
runners_data.note: Declan Carroll's five-year-old holds up and has placed twice on Good ground but those came over 6f on softer variants; Zak Wheatley is an inexperienced claimer, the OR of 65 is the lowest in the field, and without a strong gallop to close into this runner faces the tallest ask of any hold-up type here.

races.paceDynamic: The Good Biscuit is the confirmed sole front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground without being harassed. Aberama Gold, Uppercase, and Emperor Caradoc are all natural prominent types who will look to sit just off the pace and track the leader, giving the race a conventional front-three shape through the early and middle stages. Mister Sox and Sugar Baby are both genuine prominent runners by inclination but, with the prominent berths already heavily occupied, they are unlikely to secure their natural positions and have been redistributed to midfield — the field carries more pace than the race shape can accommodate. This setup — a lone uncontested leader setting a measured clip on fast ground — strongly favours horses with a prominent or just-off-the-pace profile who can travel in the slipstream and produce a clean challenge in the final furlong, rather than hold-up types who will need the pace to collapse, which it is unlikely to do from this configuration.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If The Good Biscuit dictates an unchallenged, even tempo and the prominent horses fail to produce a decisive response.
scenarios.body: The Good Biscuit sets a confident pace without pressure, conserving enough energy to maintain momentum into the final furlong on fast ground; horses sitting just off the pace in the Aberama Gold/Emperor Caradoc/Uppercase bracket are ideally positioned to mount a challenge but face a leader who never emptied the tank in the early stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Good Biscuit sets a slightly stronger-than-ideal gallop and the second-rank prominent horses swoop in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Uppercase and Aberama Gold, travelling smoothly in second gear just behind the leader, pounce as The Good Biscuit ties up close home; both carry recent winning form at 6-7f on Good ground and this scenario suits horses with a high cruising speed that can be produced in one clean effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly strong pace develops and opens a clear gap for Alfa Whiteburd or Mae Amor to close through.
scenarios.body: A genuinely hot early gallop would string the field out and create the runnel of space that true hold-up types need; Alfa Whiteburd brings two recent wins over the trip on Good ground and Mae Amor has course form, but both depend on pace they cannot manufacture themselves and this shape requires the front end to over-commit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Crowded Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Mister Sox and Sugar Baby breaks down and multiple horses contest the early lead, causing a ragged, fast-split race.
scenarios.body: A scramble for position in the first furlong would compromise Mister Sox and Sugar Baby's rhythm and could fatally unbalance those true front-runners; the beneficiaries would be hold-up horses like Alfa Whiteburd who sit out the scrimmage, though this scenario is the least likely given clear positional hierarchy in the field.

watchPoints.text: The Good Biscuit's unchallenged lead is the race's pivot — if it bowls along at a comfortable clip without being tested, the six horses in the prominent/just-off group all need to track it closely or risk being left with too much to do, making its early fractions the single most important factor in the outcome.

Mister Sox and Sugar Baby both want to race prominently but the berths are taken; watch the first furlong for any jostling or wide tracking that burns energy early, as either horse losing position cleanly could cost it any realistic chance of reaching the placed frame.

Uppercase has won both recent starts over 7f and this 6f test on quicker ground is a new question — if it fails to find the required early zip to sit up with the prominent group, its stamina-based style may leave it too far back to land a telling blow.

Alfa Whiteburd's last two wins came on Good ground at 6f and Jason Hart's strike rate with the yard warrants monitoring; if anything disrupts the front end or the pace quickens unexpectedly, it represents the most likely beneficiary among the hold-up horses.

Mae Amor's win over this course and distance earlier in the season is a meaningful data point, but its form since has deteriorated sharply — the 7-day turnaround and patchy recent figures mean it is a horse to watch in running rather than one to commit to early in the market.

races.name: Napoleons Casino Bradford Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Anzac Day
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator trained by Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill, returning after 45 days off, but the damning statistic is zero wins and zero places from eight starts on similar Good ground — a small three-runner field offers no pace to exploit and Clifford Lee will struggle to manufacture a winning move from the rear.

runners_data.name: Something
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's front runner arrives in excellent form (1W5P from 15 similar-going starts), wears a hood, and steps up to 2m1f having run consistently over shorter — Billy Garritty can dictate every yard of the race unopposed and a sustainable gallop at this trip could be decisive in a field of three.

runners_data.name: Division Day
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's four-year-old has course-relevant form over 16f+ and solid placed efforts on Soft ground, and Connor Beasley can settle prominently just off Something's lead — the key question is whether the step up to 2m1f on Good to Firm ground suits better than the Soft conditions in which it has placed over the longer trip.

races.paceDynamic: Something is the sole confirmed front runner in a three-horse field and will stride into an uncontested lead from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop over 2m1f on Good to Firm ground at Pontefract. Division Day, a prominent-style horse, will sit just behind and apply at least some positional pressure, though with only three runners the tempo is unlikely to be fierce. Anzac Day is the lone hold-up operator but has no wins or places from eight similar-going starts, making a late flourish from the rear a tall order in such a small field with no pace to hide behind. This race shape strongly favours the front-running and prominent profiles — Something can control the race entirely on its own terms, and Division Day is ideally placed to pounce if Something weakens late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Something Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Something dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and builds an unassailable lead before the home straight.
scenarios.body: Something has won and placed consistently over 12f on Good ground and now faces just two rivals, allowing Billy Garritty to set a tempo entirely on his own terms; a patient, front-running display over this longer trip suits a horse in strong recent form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Division Day Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Something's gallop is just brisk enough to drain it in the final furlong, allowing Division Day to pounce from a handy position.
scenarios.body: Division Day has placed over 2m on Soft ground and has course-and-distance relevant experience at 16f+, and Connor Beasley can ride a patient prominent race before launching a challenge; Brian Ellison has 1 winner from 23 runners in the past 14 days but Division Day's form profile makes it the most credible threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Something is genuinely strong, leaving a gap for Anzac Day to reel in the leaders deep in the straight.
scenarios.body: Anzac Day has never won or placed from eight starts on similar ground and faces a small field where there is little cover or positional advantage from hold-up tactics; this scenario requires both an uncharacteristically fast early pace and a late-race collapse from Something, making it a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Division Day disputes the early lead aggressively, creating an unexpectedly hot gallop that compromises all three runners.
scenarios.body: With only three horses, an early battle for position would be visible and damaging over 2m1f, but Division Day's prominent style does not suggest outright front-running aggression; this shape is unlikely but would most benefit any horse that settles best through the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Something's ability to control the tempo entirely unopposed is the defining factor — if Billy Garritty misjudges the pace over 2m1f on Good to Firm, Something's stamina at this trip becomes uncertain given its form has been over 12f.

Division Day's prominent style makes it the only horse with both the position and the form to threaten Something, and Connor Beasley will be watching for any sign of weakening in the final quarter-mile.
Anzac Day's record of 0 wins and 0 places from 8 similar-going starts is a significant red flag in a race where the hold-up role offers almost no tactical advantage with only three runners.

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm for the 5:15 despite the headline listing Good — this faster surface may place an additional stamina premium on Something stepping beyond its usual 12f comfort zone.
